# Vendored shadPS4

These files come from [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4), licensed GPL-2.0 (see `LICENSE`).

- **Commit:** `14ada48a1320` ("vk_rasterizer: Apply pending fast clears on FMASK decompress (#5283)")
- **Paths:** `src/common`, `src/video_core`, `src/shader_recompiler`, `LICENSE`
- **Imported with:** `python scripts/import_shadps4.py --src ../shadps4 --commit 14ada48`

`sotcgpu` (`gpu/`) builds these sources. It replaces what they take from shadPS4's `core/` with shim headers
under `gpu/shim/`.

## Local patches

Local patches are allowed: M4's AjncSystem fixes will be patches on this copy. Every patch must be listed
below: the file, what changed, and why. Re-running `import_shadps4.py` drops them, so re-apply them
afterwards.

| File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `src/video_core/amdgpu/liverpool.h`, `liverpool.cpp` | `SubmitGfx`/`SubmitAsc` take an optional `Common::UniqueFunction<void> on_done` (default empty). `GpuQueue` keeps one callback per submission (`submit_done_cbs`, pushed with the task); `Process()` pops it with the finished task and runs it on the GPU thread, outside the queue lock. | `sotcgpu_submit_gfx`/`_compute` promise a `done` callback once the command processor has consumed the buffers (the runtime advances compute ring read pointers with it). Liverpool had no completion hook. |
| `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp` | `Draw`, `DrawIndirect`, `DispatchDirect` and `DispatchIndirect` return early when `SotcSkipPipeline(pipeline)` (from `gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h`) is true. | Debug switch `SOTC_GPU_SKIP=<hash>[,<hash>...]`: drop the draws of one shader to bisect GPU hangs and rendering bugs. Inactive when the variable is unset. |
| `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_presenter.cpp` | In `Presenter::Present`, `#ifdef SOTC_NO_IMGUI`: the "Draw the game" ImGui block and `ImGui::Core::Render` are replaced by a plain fitted blit of the frame into the swapchain image (clear to black, `MakeImageBlitFit`, layouts restored to what the rest of `Present` expects). Without the define the file is unchanged. | shadPS4 draws the game frame as an ImGui image; sotcgpu compiles ImGui out (no imgui submodule, no src/imgui sources). |
| `src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h`, `buffer_cache.cpp` | `ObtainBuffer` streams a small read-only buffer only when the region is CPU-modified, and adds it to a new `streamed_ranges` set. Otherwise it binds the buffer in place from the arena. `TickFrame` calls the new `FlushStreamedRanges`, which uploads those ranges to the arena (`EnsureResident` + `SynchronizeMemory`, split at arena pages and 64 MiB). | SotC binds ~85k small read-only buffers per frame (~330 MiB). Streaming all of them each bind wrapped the 128 MiB stream buffer several times a frame, and each wrap waited for the GPU. The title ran at 4 flips/s with 1.3 GiB/s of guest copies; with the patch, copies fall to ~50 MiB/s and the title runs at 8–20 flips/s. |
| `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp` | Includes `sotc_debug.h` (`gpu/src/`). `Draw` and `DrawIndirect` call `SotcDebug::OnDraw(indirect, texture_cache, cb_descs, state.num_color_attachments, db_desc)` right after `BeginRendering`; `DispatchDirect`/`DispatchIndirect` call `SotcDebug::Count(Counter::Dispatch)`. Session 17: `DispatchDirect`/`DispatchIndirect` call `SotcDebug::SetShader(pgm_hash)` before `BindResources` and `SetShader(0)` after the dispatch (stats only: the shader that wrote a binding). | Workstream X debug tools (`gpu/src/debug_dump.cpp`): `SOTC_DUMP_RT` records the targets each draw binds, `SOTC_GPU_STATS` counts draws and dispatches. One relaxed load and a branch while the variables are unset. |
| `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_scheduler.cpp` | Includes `sotc_debug.h`. `Scheduler::Wait` counts a blocking wait (`!IsFree(tick)`) when `SotcDebug::StatsEnabled()`, under the waiting thread's `SotcDebug::WaitSite` (`CountWait`). | `SOTC_GPU_STATS`: blocking scheduler waits per second. The `IsFree` check only runs while stats are on. |
| `src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h`, `buffer_cache.cpp`, `buffer.cpp`, `fault_manager.cpp`, `texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp`, `renderer_vulkan/vk_presenter.cpp`, `amdgpu/liverpool.cpp` | Include `sotc_debug.h`. Each `Scheduler::Finish`/`Wait` caller sets a `SotcDebug::WaitScope` (buffer download in a GPU-thread fault or queued by a guest fault, `ProcessDownloadImages`, emergency GC, EOS GDS store, stream buffer, fault buffer, presenter). `BufferCache::DownloadMemory` returns whether it downloaded anything; `ReadMemory` then calls `SotcDebug::OnFaultDrain`. `ObtainBuffer` reports written bindings (`SotcDebug::OnGpuWrite`). `ProcessGraphics`/`ProcessCompute` call `SotcDebug::SetPm4(opcode)` per packet. | Session 10 drain diagnostic (`SOTC_GPU_STATS`): blocking waits by call site, and the top faulting pages with the PM4 packet behind GPU-thread faults. No behaviour change; the hooks are a TLS store or one relaxed load while stats are off. |
| `src/shader_recompiler/ir/passes/srt.h`, `flatten_extended_userdata_pass.cpp`, `src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h` | New `Shader::SrtWalkerContains(code)` (the generated walker's code range; `false` on non-x86). The walker's third argument is now `const SrtHelpers*` (`copy_window`, `resolve_table`), called through `call [r12 + offset]`; `info.h` passes `&g_srt_helpers`. `PushPtr` calls `resolve_table(rdi, bytes)` for every table whose read offsets are all immediates (`bytes` = the furthest dword or qword read); the video core installs the resolver with `SetSrtTableResolver` (default identity). New `BufferCache::IsRangeGpuWritten(addr, size)`: `gpu_modified_ranges.Intersects`, byte-precise where `IsRegionGpuModified` works in 4 KiB pages. | Session 10 drains: `sotcgpu_emulate_load` (`gpu/src/sotc_srt_load.h`) and the table resolver (`SotcSrt::ResolveTable`, through the runtime's unprotected physical backing view) let the SRT walker read CPU bytes on a GPU-blocked page without a fault or a GPU drain, as long as the bytes it reads aren't GPU-written. Emulating every faulting load alone cost 50-110k faults a second and halved the frame rate. In gameplay ~45% of all GPU drains were walker reads of a descriptor table right after a 200 KB buffer that a compute shader writes, on the same page. Unit test: `gpu/tests/test_srt_load.cpp`. |
| `src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h`, `buffer_cache.cpp`, `sotc_write_ticks.h` (new), `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_instance.h`, `vk_instance.cpp` | `SotcWriteTicks`: the scheduler tick of the newest written binding per 64 KiB (1 MiB for bindings over 16 MiB), noted in `ObtainBuffer`. `DownloadMemory` copies data written in an already-submitted batch with `SotcSideCopy` (a one-shot command buffer and fence; on a second graphics-family queue it waits on the timeline semaphore at the write tick, otherwise on the graphics queue behind a leading barrier) instead of `Scheduler::Finish`; data written in the batch being recorded still takes `Finish`. `SOTC_SIDE_READBACK=0` turns it off. The instance creates up to 2 queues of the graphics family (`GetSotcReadbackQueue`). Stats: downloads by write tick (in batch / submitted / done / unknown) and side copies. | Session 10: ~75% of the remaining downloads were of data the GPU had finished writing, but `Finish` flushed the batch being recorded and waited for all of it (~4 ms each). After bbport's `GpuWriteTicks` and `FastReadback`. Unit test: `gpu/tests/test_write_ticks.cpp`. |
| `src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h`, `buffer_cache.cpp`, `src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp` | Hot flush: when a fault needed GPU data still in the batch being recorded, `ReadMemory` remembers the 256-byte line (`sotc_hot_lines`, at most 256). A later written binding over a hot line sets a flush request; `DispatchDirect`/`DispatchIndirect` then submit the batch right after the dispatch (`Scheduler::Flush`, no wait). `SOTC_HOT_FLUSH=0` turns it off. With stats on, `DownloadMemory` compares the downloaded bytes with the CPU copy (`SotcDebug::OnDownloadCompare`). | Session 10: SotC computes per-view constants with a dispatch and the next draws' SRT walkers read them, each a `Scheduler::Finish` (~4 ms). | `src/shader_recompiler/ir/passes/srt.h`, `flatten_extended_userdata_pass.cpp`, `resource_patching_pass.cpp`, `info.h`, `backend/spirv/emit_spirv_context_get_set.cpp` | **Runtime-indexed ReadConst** (after AjncSystem's SotC build, commit `609b4dd2cc`). When the SRT walker can't compute a ReadConst's offset (a loop counter: `ComputeOffset ... Phi`), it copies a window of that table (`ReadConstDynamicWindowDwords` = 4096 dwords, one per table) into the flattened buffer through `SrtCopyWindow` (`CopySparseMemory`; the zero block for a null pointer), and flags the ReadConst `ReadConstDynamicWindowFlag | window`. `EmitReadConst` loads `flatbuf[window + min(index, 4095)]`. The walker takes the helper as a third argument (`PFN_SrtWalker`, kept in r12), since walker code is cached. A sharp read with a runtime index stays `UNKNOWN_LOCATION`. Each such shader logs `SRT walker: N runtime-indexed reads from a window in shader 0x...`. | Session 8, bug (c): with direct memory access off (our default) those reads kept flags 0 and loaded `flatbuf[0]` (user data s0) for every index. SotC's depth-of-field shaders (the 89-offset family, e.g. `0x5d6ab77`) loop over 272-byte table entries, so DOF drew large smeared blocks. AjncSystem's 512-dword window is too small for `0xf94d23d4` (loops from byte 1712). Unit test: `gpu/tests/test_recompiler.cpp` (`TestSrtDynamicIndex`). |

On a failed `allocateMemory` / sparse `createBuffer` / `vmaCreateBuffer` / `vmaCreateImage`, log a `[vram] ... failed` line with the request (size, address range, image extent/format) before the existing assert. | Same: VRAM budget diagnostics. | `src/video_core/buffer_cache/residency_allocator.h`, `residency_allocator.cpp` (new), `buffer_cache.h`, `buffer_cache.cpp`, `renderer_vulkan/vk_platform.h` | Opt-in: `SOTC_RESIDENCY=chunks`. The default (`legacy`) keeps shadPS4's one `vkAllocateMemory` per `EnsureResident` call, because chunks stalled or crashed in 2 of 3 intro runs. New `VideoCore::ResidencyAllocator`: 256 MiB device-memory chunks (dedicated chunk when a request is larger) carved into block-granular slices; best fit, else free ranges largest-first (at most 16 slices), else a new chunk; `Free` and `ReleaseEmptyChunks` for eviction. Vulkan-free core with injected allocate/free callbacks. `EnsureResident` allocates its gaps from it and emits one sparse bind + one `Backing` per gap/slice piece instead of one `vkAllocateMemory` per call. `~BufferCache` waits for the device to go idle; the chunks are freed after the arenas. `SotcDiag` gains `arena_chunks`/`arena_chunk_bytes`; `arena_resident_bytes`/`arena_allocations` now mean bytes in slices / chunk allocations (`PublishResidencyStats`). | Workstream R part 1 (`docs/next/r.md`): the ~230 s `ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory` came after 1,700–2,400 residency allocations against NVIDIA's `maxMemoryAllocationCount` of 4096. Unit test: `gpu/tests/test_residency.cpp`. |
| `src/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.h`, `texture_cache.cpp`, `sotc_gc_policy.h` (new) | `GarbageCollectImages` is rewritten around `VideoCore::SotcGc` (Vulkan-free, header-only). Thresholds are 50/70/85 % of `Instance::GetTotalMemoryBudget()` (normal/pressured/critical; idle below). One pass per tick walks the LRU oldest first. Images whose guest bytes are current go after 120/30/8 ticks unused. **Tiled GPU-written images (`SafeToDownload`) go without a download** after 1800/300/60 ticks. Linear GPU-written ones are downloaded, then freed, under pressure (as before). At most 8/32/128 frees and 4096 visits per tick; kept images no longer use up the free budget. Totals go to `SotcDiag::gc_*`. New `SotcPublishImageBreakdown` (every ~10 s, GPU thread) writes `SotcDiag::gc_breakdown`: live images by age bucket, targets / texture-only / tiled GPU-written, images sharing a base address, view count, the 4 largest. shadPS4's threshold members are still computed but no longer used for images. | Workstream T (`docs/next/t.md`): VRAM grew past the 6 GB card's budget (1,392 live images, 3.8 GiB at 580 s). shadPS4 never freed tiled GPU-written images (every render and depth target). It also counted them against the per-tick deletion budget, so a few at the LRU head stopped the GC for good, and its trigger is 0 on cards under 8 GB. Freeing without a download doesn't change what the CPU sees: tiled images are never written back to guest memory. A re-created image uploads the guest bytes. Unit test: `gpu/tests/test_gc_policy.cpp`. |

| `src/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.h`, `texture_cache.cpp`, `sotc_gc_policy.h`, `image.cpp`, `buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h`, `buffer_cache.cpp`, `renderer_vulkan/vk_platform.h` | Emergency image GC. On `ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory` in `EnsureResident` (legacy `allocateMemory` or the chunk allocator) or in `UniqueImage::Create` (`vmaCreateImage`, through the `SotcDiag::emergency_gc` hook the texture cache installs), `TextureCache::SotcEmergencyCollect` frees images not used in this GC tick, oldest first (`SotcGc::Level::Emergency`: age >= 1, GPU-written tiled images too, no downloads), until `EmergencyTarget(request)` = max(2x request, 256 MiB). Images `FindImage` is resolving are pinned (`sotc_gc_pinned`). It runs only on the GC thread and never nested. Then `scheduler.Finish()` + `PopPendingOperations()` so the frees reach the driver. The caller retries once and asserts only if that fails. Counters `gc_emergency_*`. **Images use `VMA_ALLOCATION_CREATE_DEDICATED_MEMORY_BIT`.** `BufferCache::SotcPublishArenaCoverage` (called with the image breakdown) publishes `arena_ranges_bytes`/`arena_image_bytes`: arena resident bytes inside live images' guest ranges (`SotcGc::IntersectBytes`, `AnalyzeOverlap`'s new `unions` output). | Session 5 (`docs/NEXT.md`): VRAM exhaustion asserted. With VMA's shared blocks a freed image only left a hole: the first emergency pass freed 259 MiB, device usage didn't move, and the retry failed. Dedicated allocations return the memory immediately and cut steady-state heap0 usage below the budget (no emergency pass needed in a 370 s gameplay run). Unit test: `gpu/tests/test_gc_policy.cpp`. |

Unit test: `gpu/tests/test_guest_hash.cpp`. |

When a patch changes the SPIR-V that `shader_recompiler` generates, bump `kPipelineCacheVersion` in
`gpu/src/sotcgpu.cpp`. The pipeline cache only checks shadPS4's own version numbers, so without the bump it
would keep loading shaders compiled before the patch.

Everything else shadPS4 takes from its `core/`, `imgui/`, Tracy and Abseil is replaced by headers under
`gpu/shim/` (see `docs/m3/gl.md`), not by edits here. `common/logging/log.cpp` and `common/path_util.cpp` are
not compiled; `gpu/src/log.cpp` and `gpu/src/path_util.cpp` replace them.
